title: Sector Rotation by Factor Model and Fundamental Analysis

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper constructs sector rotation strategies using momentum factors (past 1-12 month returns excluding the most recent month), short-term reversion factors (negative cumulative returns over 5 to 55 days), and a neural network model taking fundamental factors (such as PE, PB, EV/Sales, EV/EBIT, dividend yield, margins, ROA, ROE) as inputs. Portfolios are formed by ranking sectors cross-sectionally and taking long/short positions in the top and bottom sectors on a monthly or quarterly basis.
extraction.data_period: 2002 to February 2022 (and September 2020 to September 2021 for the neural network test set)
extraction.universe: 11 MSCI level one sectors using S&P 500 GICS Indices

key_findings: Momentum and short-term reversion factors exhibit significant predictive power in sector rotation, with MOM 7M and Rev 30D showing strong risk-adjusted performance.
Fundamental metrics such as P/E, P/B, EV/Sales, and margins reveal distinct sector characteristics (e.g., Real Estate being overvalued, IT and Consumer Staples exhibiting strong profitability).
A neural network model using neutralized fundamental indicators achieves a 64% prediction accuracy on the test set.
Trading based on the neural network probability outputs yields a Sharpe ratio of 2.21 on the test set from September 2020 to September 2021.
limitations: Small sample size for quarterly fundamental data limiting the training size.
Factor neutralization issues where different sectors possess inner trends of higher exposures.
Model may not be applicable on a wider range of time because it was trained and tested on only the most recent five years.
